Regularized Regression Priors

Source: R/priors.R
prior_regularized.Rd

Set ridge, lasso, or horseshoe priors for moderator or scale regression coefficients. A named group in prior_mods or prior_scale can share one shrinkage scale across its terms. The intercept retains its own prior. For a centered factor, lasso shrinks the length of the fitted contrast vector and horseshoe assigns one local scale to that vector. Treatment and independent contrasts have coordinate-wise shrinkage. The scale is in fitted coefficient units, so the same scale can give different prior spreads for factor-level effects under different contrasts. An interaction inherits its factors' fitted codings. To change the coding of a factor in the interaction, specify it on that factor's main effect.

Usage

prior_regularized(
  family,
  scale,
  terms = NULL,
  slab_scale = NULL,
  slab_df = 4,
  contrast = NULL
)

Arguments

family

One of "ridge", "lasso", and "horseshoe".

scale

A positive number fixing the global scale, or a proper scalar continuous prior with positive support from which to learn it. The scale is in fitted coefficient units. For a single lasso coefficient it is the Laplace scale. For a centered factor it scales the Euclidean norm in the group-lasso density.

terms

Optional character vector of fixed-effect term labels. Place a group under its own name in the formula prior list. Omitting terms selects the non-intercept terms without a prior of their own. Separate named groups have independent scales, even if they use the same scale prior. A multi-column term uses its fitted coefficient basis.

slab_scale

Positive scale of the Student-t slab for the regularized horseshoe. The default NULL selects the classical horseshoe.

slab_df

Positive degrees of freedom of the Student-t slab.

contrast

Optional factor coding, one of "treatment", "independent", "meandif" or "orthonormal". With NULL, JAGS_formula() uses treatment coding by default and a calling model can supply its factor coding.

Value

With numeric scale and omitted terms, ridge and lasso return ordinary scalar priors accepted by prior_spike_and_slab() and prior_mixture(). Otherwise the result declares a coefficient group for JAGS_formula(). is.prior.regularized() identifies group declarations. is.prior.regularized_term() identifies coefficient priors bound to a group.

See also

prior_specification(), BayesTools::prior_regularized()

Examples

global <- prior("cauchy", list(0, 0.2), list(0, Inf))
moderator_priors <- list(
  shrinkage = prior_regularized("horseshoe", terms = c("age", "dose"),
                               scale = global, slab_scale = 2, slab_df = 4)
)
# Jointly shrink the contrasts of a design factor in a meta-regression.
design_priors <- list(
  design_group = prior_regularized("lasso", terms = "design", scale = 0.3,
                                   contrast = "meandif")
)
